judgment_calls_flagged_for_reviewer: 6 of the 38 markers (audit.ex:314; definitions.ex:1167, 1178, and 1194; identity.ex:771; instances.ex:316 -- exact post-insertion line numbers) sit inside plain Elixir `#` comment blocks, not a @moduledoc heredoc or a .md file -- a context the design doc (built around moduledoc prose/table/bullet and Markdown citations) does not explicitly address. Inserting the bare marker line there would not be valid Elixir syntax outside a string/heredoc and would break compilation. I prefixed those specific marker lines with '# ' (matching the surrounding comment style) so the file stays syntactically valid while the marker text remains substring-greppable by the design's own regex (grep matches the substring regardless of a leading '# '). Files affected: lib/letflow/routers/audit.ex (1 marker), lib/letflow/routers/definitions.ex (3 markers), lib/letflow/routers/identity.ex (1 marker), lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex (1 marker). Flagging for REVIEWER sign-off since this is a small extension of the design's own convention, not something the design doc itself resolved.

definitions.ex: the heading line '## Two different R-Co files are called `validation.zig`. They are unrelated.' itself contains a .zig substring; treated as its own single-line citation unit (marker placed directly above the heading), separate from the two list bullets immediately below it (each bullet also cites a distinct validation.zig file and got its own marker). Flagging in case REVIEWER reads the design's 'paragraph' rule as intending the heading+list to be one combined unit instead.
